items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: or maybe now I’m doing a Marvin Gaye tune or a Stevie Wonder song.

ctx.x: No. No. I just appreciate the fact that that person or artist is still trying to push the envelope and is still trying to find something different or another facet of their creative nature. So right, Coltrane in ’57 is very different than ’66, but it’s still Coltrane. So I appreciate the ride. I really do. So I don’t know, I get a lot of people who are going well Wayne Shorter sure doesn’t sound like he did in 1961. He’s not supposed to. That’s like me saying well man, some of your high school friends say well…

able to appreciate that for what it is. I can’t go into an Italian restaurant and say man this doesn’t taste like soul food. It’s not supposed to. And so I think as I’ve gotten older I’ve been able to — and I’m still a young man but I’m getting to a point where everybody has all these things to offer. There was a period where I said you know what? I want to play some of the music that influenced me. So you hear me doing [sings] Wake up everybody/no more sleep. So I’m doing that kind of music, where before, when I…
It takes every kind of people, right?
